title: Academic manager jobs in Vietnam: the teacher career ladder
description: Teacher to senior teacher, DOS, examiner or trainer in Vietnam: what each step needs, Delta and CELTA costs, published pay, and the work-permit catch.
h1: Career paths for English teachers in Vietnam: from the classroom to academic manager, examiner or trainer
intro: Foreign English teachers in Vietnam usually move from classroom teacher to senior teacher, then director of studies or academic manager, with examining and teacher training alongside. Most steps ask for a CELTA or equivalent and two to five years of documented experience; CELTA assessors need a Delta-level diploma. International schools are a separate track that needs a teaching licence such as QTS. Few employers publish senior pay, and a promotion that changes your job title needs a new work permit.
keyPoints: **Examining usually comes first**: Cambridge speaking examiners need about 1,800 teaching hours (roughly 2 years full-time); IELTS examiners need a degree, a TEFL/TESOL and 3–5 years, and in Vietnam are recruited by the British Council and IDP.

**The Delta gates Cambridge assessor roles**: a CELTA assessor needs Delta Modules One to Three plus 5+ years. We found no Delta course advertised in Vietnam for 2026–27, so teachers based in Saigon generally study by distance; IH London lists distance Module 2 at £2,165 plus a £193 Cambridge fee.

**A promotion is a work-permit event**: moving from teacher to DOS or academic manager needs a new permit even with the same employer (Decree 219/2025/ND-CP, Art 20(2)), and working for a second employer needs a permit for that employer (Art 20(1)).

**International schools are a separate track**: they want a teaching licence (QTS, a US state licence or home-country certification) plus 2–3 years. iQTS confers English QTS and is done where you live and work; an iPGCE may not lead to QTS.

**Your own centre is a company project, not a side line**: foreigners cannot register a household business, and an owner is exempt from a work permit only with a capital contribution of {{vnd:3000000000}} or more.

sections.title: The career ladder for English teachers in Vietnam

blocks.text: Promotion in Vietnam is not a published pay scale. It is a series of gates: a qualification, a number of documented hours or years, or a licence. The table pulls together what exam boards and employers ask for. Pay is shown only where an employer, an exam board or a job ad publishes it, as of October 2026.

blocks.text: The experience thresholds combine exam-board criteria with a 2026 job-board guide; there is no official promotion timeline ([Vietnam Teaching Jobs](https://blog.vietnamteachingjobs.com/average-salary-esl-teachers-vietnam/), [Cambridge English](https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/teaching-english/professional-development/become-a-cambridge-english-examiner/)). International-school pay comes from [TeachAcrossAsia](https://teachacrossasia.com/teaching-locations/teaching-jobs-in-vietnam/) and [Spill.org](https://spill.org/en/guides/ho-chi-minh-city-vietnam-expat-guide), and the corporate figure is a single expired ad, so treat both as indications rather than offers.

At centres, **ads rarely show what experience is worth**: they publish new-teacher rates and 'up to' ceilings, not pay scales. Wall Street English is one of the few to mention an annual performance-based raise ([the ad](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/ho-chi-minh-city-part-time-native-english-teachers-2)). A full-time centre load is about 78–95 contact hours a month, which at {{vnd:450000-550000}} an hour comes to roughly {{vnd:35000000-52000000}} gross a month (load from [a 2024 Apollo listing](https://www.seriousteachers.com/job_details/278256/0/vietnamesl-teacher-teachers-needed-now-in-vietnam-vietnam)). The full picture, including tax and bonuses, is in [English teacher salary in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-salary-in-vietnam).

To look for senior and academic posts, eno.vn's [teaching jobs page](/jobs-vietnam-expats) gathers postings from job boards and schools' own careers pages, and a linked posting opens the original, where you apply; eno.vn has not verified the employers behind them, and you should never pay to get a job. The [school directory](/schools) lists Ho Chi Minh City employers, international and bilingual schools and universities among them, with teacher reviews where they exist (most have few or none yet). To be found for the next role, a free teacher profile started at [teacher.eno.vn](https://teacher.eno.vn) shows your experience and qualifications as you add them, such as Delta modules or examiner status; schools, centres and anyone else signed in to eno.vn can message you, and your phone number, email and CV stay hidden until you choose to share them in that chat.

sections.title: The Delta: what it costs and where to take it

blocks.text: The Cambridge Delta, or an equivalent, is the qualification that gates Cambridge assessor roles. A CELTA assessor needs at least 5 years' varied, current ELT experience, Delta Modules One to Three (or the DTEFLA, Trinity DipTESOL or equivalent) and ongoing delivery of at least two CELTA courses a year; Delta Module Two assessors need the Delta or equivalent and recent experience as a Module Two tutor or in-service trainer. Both are recruited only in specific campaigns ([Cambridge English](https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/teaching-english/professional-development/become-a-cambridge-english-examiner/)). A common route, not an official one, is senior teacher, then trainer-in-training at a CELTA centre, then assessor.

We found **no Delta course advertised in Vietnam for 2026–27**: International House's course finder lists only CELTA intakes for Apollo IH Ho Chi Minh City ([IH Ho Chi Minh City](https://ihteachenglish.com/school/ih-ho-chi-minh-city/)). Ask Apollo IH, ILA and British Council Vietnam directly before you plan around a local course. A common pattern among Saigon-based teachers is to take Modules One and Three online part-time while working, then Module Two either online, with lessons observed at their own school, or face to face abroad during a break. Check each provider's rules on local tutors and observation.

blocks.caption: International House London Delta fees from its 2026 price list (table headed 'DELTA 2027'), paid in pounds to IH London; Cambridge assessment fees are on top of tuition
rows: Integrated online Modules One to Three

blocks.text: Compare totals, not tuition alone ([IH London price list](https://www.ihlondon.com/?p=74058)). The Module Three ELT Management option is worth a look if a DOS or academic manager post is your target.
Is the Delta worth it if you are staying in Vietnam?

Not for the hourly rate on its own. We found no 2025–2026 Saigon ad that publishes a pay premium for the Delta; the only hard figure is old: a 2019 British Council summer school in the city paid Delta holders about 13% more than CELTA holders. **What the Delta buys is access**: Cambridge assessor roles require it or an equivalent, and senior and DOS posts are commonly built around it. Ask your employer to fund or part-fund it in return for a written training contract that sets how long you stay and what you repay if you leave early (the only basis the Labour Code gives for repaying costs beyond the Art. 40 amounts), and agree in advance that you can teach observed Module Two lessons at your school.
CELTA first, if you do not have it yet

Most steps above start from a CELTA or equivalent; the exceptions are entry-level centre teaching (a TEFL), examining (a recognised teaching qualification, or a TEFL/TESOL for IELTS) and international schools (a teaching licence). Apollo IH Ho Chi Minh City charges {{vnd:42000000}} including Cambridge fees, or {{vnd:39500000}} if you pay at least 6 weeks before the start. The course is full-time over 4 weeks, 9:00–17:30, with intakes on 16 November–11 December 2026 (its early price closed around 5 October) and 4–29 January 2027 ([IH course page](https://www.ihteachenglish.com/course/3726)). IH pages give the centre as District 3; since July 2025 official addresses use new ward names, so confirm the address before you book somewhere to stay. How the CELTA compares with a cheaper TEFL is covered in [TEFL, TESOL or CELTA for Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/tefl-tesol-and-celta-for-vietnam).

sections.title: MA TESOL, university jobs and young-learner certificates

blocks.text: MA TESOL or Delta first?

A long-standing forum saying among teachers is that 'an MA gets you the job, a Delta helps you do it' ([Dave's ESL Cafe](https://forums.eslcafe.com/job/viewtopic.php?p=1210997)). Some UK MA TESOL programmes give credit for the Delta, so taking the Delta first and the MA second can save time and fees. Check the university's credit-transfer rules before you enrol in either.

The MA matters most for universities. RMIT Vietnam's 2026 Educator role, paid by the hour, asks for a bachelor's degree, a CELTA or equivalent and at least 3 years' verifiable post-CELTA experience, with a relevant master's desirable; non-native speakers need IELTS Academic 8.0 with no band below 7.5 ([RMIT position description](https://www.rmit.edu.au/content/dam/rmit/au/en/careers/position-descriptions/vietnam/JD-Educator%20July%202026.pdf)). Vietnam's new [Law on Higher Education 125/2025/QH15](https://luatvietnam.vn/can-bo-cong-chuc/cac-chuc-danh-giang-vien-dai-hoc-theo-luat-giao-duc-dai-hoc-2025-566-106356-article.html), in force since 1 January 2026, ties lecturer standards to the Law on Teachers; the minimum degree it sets for foreign English lecturers has not been confirmed.

The work permit adds a layer. Decree 219/2025/ND-CP asks experts working in education to prove the qualification standard set by education law, including the Higher Education Law, and tasks the Ministry of Education and Training with guiding which diplomas count ([Decree 219, Art 19(3)(đ)](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html)). A school or university post can therefore need different papers from centre work. If you are paying for an MA partly to qualify for one, ask the target employer in writing whether it will accept that degree, online or not, for your permit.
The CELTA YL extension no longer exists

Cambridge discontinued the Young Learner extension to CELTA, along with TKT: KAL and TKT Practical, from December 2016, and points teachers to TKT: Young Learners instead ([Cambridge English](https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/teaching-english/teaching-courses-and-modules-discontinued)). Trinity's TYLEC is the usual substitute certificate, and IH London runs a 1-week Teaching Young Learners course for £663 (July 2027 dates). Job ads or advice that still ask for a 'CELTA YL' are out of date. Much centre teaching in Saigon is with children, so this can matter early; see [teaching young learners in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-young-learners-in-vietnam).

sections.title: How to become an IELTS or Cambridge examiner in Vietnam

blocks.text: Examining is usually the first step up a teacher can reach, after about two years of full-time teaching. Cambridge's threshold is stated in hours and IELTS's in years, which is why logging your hours from day one pays off.

rows: The test centre: in Vietnam, the British Council or IDP
Undergraduate degree or equivalent, a TEFL/TESOL qualification, 3–5 years' teaching

Local authorised Cambridge exam centres (Cambridge does not employ speaking examiners)
First degree, a recognised teaching qualification, recent experience ideally equal to at least 1,800 hours
The degree or the qualification, not both, can be waived with ideally 3,000+ hours and positive references; Induction, Training and Certification modules come before live examining

blocks.text: Sources: [IELTS](https://ielts.org/organisations/ielts-for-organisations/ielts-for-your-sector/ielts-for-teachers/become-an-ielts-examiner) and [Cambridge English](https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/teaching-english/professional-development/become-a-cambridge-english-examiner/). **No examiner pay rate is published for Vietnam**: each test centre sets its own pay and working hours, so ask the British Council or IDP for their per-session fees before you plan around the income.

Examining is paid work for an organisation other than your employer, and a Vietnamese work permit covers one employer: working for a second employer needs a separate permit for that employer (Decree 219, Art 20(1)), and since 10 September 2026 a worker without a valid permit is fined {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} and may be deported under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP ([Sức khỏe & Đời sống](https://suckhoedoisong.vn/tu-10-9-2026-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-se-bi-phat-neu-khong-co-giay-phep-lao-dong-169260824224738.htm)). Before you accept sessions, ask the test centre in writing how your work permit is covered, and check that your main contract allows outside work. The classroom side of IELTS is in [teaching IELTS in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-ielts-in-vietnam).

sections.title: Moving from a centre to an international school

blocks.text: International schools are the one move a TEFL, CELTA or Delta does not unlock. At general schools licensed as foreign-invested, teachers need at least a university pedagogy (teaching) degree or equivalent ([Decree 86/2018, Art 38](https://vcci.com.vn/legal-document/nghi-dinh-862018nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-hop-tac-dau-tu-cua-nuoc-ngoai-trong-linh-vuc-giao-duc)), and schools meet that with recognised credentials such as PGCE with QTS, a US state licence or home-country certification, plus 2–3 years' experience. Hiring, packages and where schools advertise are in [international school jobs in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/international-school-jobs-in-vietnam).

The usual route from a centre is a teaching licence. iQTS, which the UK Department for Education treats as equivalent to English QTS, takes about a year of mostly online study while you work here if a school will host your placement; do not assume an iPGCE gives QTS. The routes, providers and costs are compared in [international school jobs in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/international-school-jobs-in-vietnam#moving-from-esl).

sections.title: Promotions, job changes and the work permit

blocks.text: Your work permit names your employer and your job position, so career moves are paperwork moves. Under [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://congbaocdn.chinhphu.vn/CongBaoCP/VanBan/2025/8/45798/58141-1-20251073-1074219-2025-nd-cp.pdf), in force since 7 August 2025:

items: **A promotion that changes the job position or form of work** on your permit, for example teacher to DOS or academic manager, needs a new permit even with the same employer (Art 20(2)). The file is shorter, with proof of the new position.

**A new employer** needs a new permit, even for the same job (Art 20(1)). Since Decision 346/QĐ-BNV (24 March 2026) you re-submit your degree and experience proof in this case ([EY](https://www.ey.com/en_vn/technical/tax/tax-and-law-updates/decision-346-qd-bnv-on-the-amendment-and-supplementation-of-administrative-procedures-for-foreign-employees-working-in-vietnam)).

**A management post** may be filed in a different category: the executive-director category needs at least 3 years' experience in the relevant field (Art 3(2)(b)). Teachers are normally filed as experts, which needs a bachelor's degree plus at least 2 years' relevant experience (Art 3(3)(a)).
**Each permit lasts up to 2 years** and can be extended once by up to 2 years; after that you need a new permit.

In Ho Chi Minh City the Department of Home Affairs (Sở Nội vụ) handles permits for practically every language centre and school ([Decision 6093/QĐ-UBND](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/quyet-dinh-6093-qd-ubnd-tp-ho-chi-minh-2026-cong-bo-danh-muc-thu-tuc-hanh-chinh-sua-doi-bo-sung-448197-d2.html)). The employer files, and the employer and the authority have the final word on your case.

blocks.title: Do not start the new role on the old permit
blocks.text: Working outside what your permit covers is a ground for revoking it (Decree 219, Art 30), and a permit stops being valid when your contract no longer matches it (Labour Code, Art 156). Before you accept a DOS title, a second employer or examining sessions, ask HR in writing which permit will cover the work and when it will be filed. The full process is in [the work permit guide](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers).

items.title: Log your contact hours from day one
items.text: Keep timetables, payslips and reference letters. Examiner criteria are stated in hours, and senior posts ask for documented years.

items.title: Get an experience letter before you leave any job
items.text: Signed and stamped on letterhead, stating your job title, start and end dates and whether you were full-time. For a work permit, experience abroad is proved by a written confirmation from the foreign employer (Art 19(3)(a)), while experience in Vietnam counts through your earlier Vietnamese work permits; letters from Vietnamese employers still serve as references for examiner and senior applications.

items.title: Keep a copy of every Vietnamese work permit and contract
items.text: Earlier Vietnamese work permits count as proof of experience for your next one. When a permit stops being valid, the employer must collect it and return it to the authority within 15 days, so hand it to HR and keep a photocopy.

items.title: Prepare letters from employers abroad
items.text: Since 11 September 2026, documents from Apostille member countries need an apostille; others still need consular legalisation (Decree 293/2026/ND-CP). Germany, Austria and Czechia objected to Vietnam's accession, and the Convention takes effect for Thailand only on 28 February 2027, so experience letters from employers in those countries still need consular legalisation. Either way, add a certified Vietnamese translation.

blocks.text: Experience letters and the rest of the exit paperwork are in [leaving Vietnam: a checklist for teachers](/teach-in-vietnam/leaving-vietnam-checklist-for-teachers).

sections.title: Starting your own teaching business: the legal limits

blocks.text: The route most teachers imagine, freelancing and then opening a small centre, does not exist in that form for foreigners. The household business (hộ kinh doanh), Vietnam's simplest sole-trader form, is reserved for Vietnamese citizens under [Decree 168/2025/ND-CP](https://hethongphapluat.com/nghi-dinh-168-2025-nd-cp-ve-dang-ky-doanh-nghiep/dieu-82), as it was under the decree before it. A foreigner who wants to run a tutoring business [needs a company and the investment procedures](https://luatvietnam.vn/doanh-nghiep/nguoi-nuoc-ngoai-co-duoc-thanh-lap-ho-kinh-doanh-561-31579-article.html).

blocks.text: Sources: [Decree 219, Arts 7 and 9](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html) and [Luật Việt An](https://luatvietan.vn/cac-truong-hop-khong-thuoc-dien-cap-giay-phep-lao-dong.html) on the owner exemption. A foreign-owned language centre is also foreign investment in education. Decrees 124/2024 and 125/2024, in force since 20 November 2024, set the conditions, and Decree 124 requires foreign investors to complete at least 50% of total capital within five years of the operating licence ([KPMG](https://kpmg.com/vn/en/home/insights/2024/11/legal-update-decree-124-and-125-updates.html)).

In practice, most teachers who go independent either join a Vietnamese-owned centre as academic director or partner, with the centre sponsoring the work permit, or set up a company with enough capital to qualify for the owner's exemption. **Have a licensed Vietnamese law firm scope it before you commit money**; this guide explains the rules, it is not legal advice. Why freelance tutoring is not a workaround is covered in [private tutoring and online teaching in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/private-tutoring-and-online-teaching-in-vietnam).

faqs.q: How much does a director of studies or academic manager earn in Saigon?
faqs.a: Language centres do not publish DOS or academic-manager pay, so it is negotiated case by case; get the offer in writing and ask whether it is gross or net. The published figures at the top of the market are from international schools, where one 2026 guide puts heads of department at US$3,800-5,500 a month and leadership at US$6,000-12,000 or more.

faqs.q: How long does it take to go from teacher to DOS in Vietnam?
faqs.a: There is no official timeline. Senior posts typically ask for 2-5 years of documented experience, and a DOS post at a premium centre for 5 or more years plus management experience, usually with the Delta.

faqs.q: Can I do the Delta in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: We found no Delta course advertised in Vietnam for 2026-27, only CELTA intakes, so most teachers in Saigon study by distance and arrange observed Module Two lessons at their own school or travel for a face-to-face course. Ask Apollo IH, ILA and British Council Vietnam directly, as this can change.

faqs.q: Can I teach at a university in Vietnam with a bachelor's degree and a CELTA?
faqs.a: Some university roles accept it: RMIT's 2026 Educator role asks for a bachelor's, a CELTA or equivalent and 3 years after the CELTA, with a master's desirable. The minimum degree for foreign lecturers under the 2025 Higher Education Law has not been confirmed, so ask the university what it will file for your work permit.

faqs.q: Does an online MA TESOL count for a work permit or a university job in Vietnam?
faqs.a: No published rule settles it. Ask the employer, in writing and before you enrol, whether it accepts that degree for hiring and whether it will file it for your work permit.

faqs.q: Will my years teaching in Vietnam count for my next work permit?
faqs.a: Yes, through your earlier Vietnamese work permits, which Decree 219 accepts as proof of experience. Keep a copy of every permit and contract, and ask each employer for an experience letter to use as a reference.
